set.approach: From Telluride drive south toward Lizard Head Pass, then continue south past the pass to a dirt road signed for the Cross Mountain trailhead and park there. Take the trail to a pass between Cross Mountain and Lizard Head, go up the grass shoulder, then follow the climber's trail to the base and around to the right for the south-face routes. This line replaces the third pitch of the standard route, on the southwest side of the summit block, to the right of the standard chimney, starting at a small V-shaped notch above the second-pitch talus.
set.descent_text: The route ends at the chains where the standard third pitch ends; from there the descent is by rappel with some downclimbing.

review.notes: Route page for the variation's position and finish at the rappel chains; area page for the trailhead and trail, and the rappel descent.

set.approach: Begin at Summit Lake, descend to the upper Chicago Lake and contour east along the foot of the cliff to the route you want. A big left-facing cleft divides the main wall above the lakes, and this line runs up the middle of the wall.

review.notes: Area page for the approach; route page is a placeholder stating only the line.

set.approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and climb the short talus slope directly to the wall. The route starts from the midway ledge: reach the ledge by one of the ways described for the Dark Tower, or climb the lower pitches of Raise the Roof. Then walk left along the base of the wall to a short splitter crack at the base of the little gully on the mini-tower to the right of the Dark Tower, beside the big gully next to it.
set.descent_text: Descend the East gully. Walk down the slope of Thatchtop staying fairly close to the North Face; at treeline look for cairns that lead down a big scree and talus slope, and bear a little toward skier's left near the bottom to enter a smaller gully with some third-class steps down to the ground.

review.notes: Route page for the start and descent; North Face area page for the Loch approach.

set.approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and climb the short talus slope directly to the north face. The Dark Tower is the largest tower on the left of the face, with the Deep Freeze cleft to its left and the Necrophilia gully to its right. The start is in a steep right-facing corner to the left of the giant corner that lies below the left side of the tower; the line crosses that big corner near its top and gains the large ledge system.
set.descent_text: To escape from the midway ledge, head left on the ledge toward the Deep Freeze gully, downclimb several tiers on its left side to a rappel anchor, and rappel to the ground near the start. Continuing up means joining the prow of the Dark Tower.

review.notes: Route page for start, ledge and escape; North Face area page for the Loch approach and layout.

set.approach: Park at Glacier Gorge, or at Bear Lake if that lot is full, and walk in to the Loch. Go around the west side of the lake, cross the stream, and head up the short talus slope to the north face. The tower sits on the large ledge that crosses the face at one-third to half height, so first reach the ledge: climb the right-angling weakness to the right of Necrophilia, climb the lower pitches of Raise the Roof and walk left, or take the Direct Start. Then find the prow with the splitter crack.
set.descent_text: Rappel off the back of the tower to a level area, then either scramble up to the ridgeline for one of the walk-offs or cross to the head of the Deep Freeze rappels.

review.notes: Route page for access to the ledge, the prow and the descent; North Face area page for the Loch approach.

set.approach: Leave the car at the Willow Lake trailhead in the town of Crestone and follow the South Crestone trail up to just before the large open meadow, where the trail switchbacks around a big buried boulder. Look left (north) to the group of towers: on the far left is a face of polished conglomerate with a straight splitter crack down the middle and three car-sized pegmatite boulders on its upper right. Leave the trail there, go north through the talus by the easiest line, and the flat terrace at the base is the place to start.
set.descent_text: Scramble north down into the notch that joins the tower to the hillside; the step off the summit and the final step into the saddle are low fifth class, where a belay from a partner is reasonable. From the saddle, descend the gully on the west side, wrapping back around the tower to the start.

review.notes: Route page for the approach, landmarks and descent; area page agrees on the leave-the-trail point.

set.approach: It climbs the south-facing Chessboard Wall, high in Oil Creek on Pikes Peak's southwest side. The lower Oil Creek valley is private land, so work out a line through national forest that avoids trespass. One public-land option follows the trail to Horse Thief Park and heads east up the drainage above the falls. Look for the conspicuous arching crack that sweeps left to right.

review.notes: Route page gives the wall, line and access caution; area page is nearly empty.

set.approach: This crag lies in the Abyss Lake basin on the Mount Evans side. It is reached by descending from the road and traversing south, nearly as far as Corner Buttress and the Wind Tower. The line follows broken cracks, one of them an offwidth, on the west-facing left side of a huge, wide-angled open book.

review.notes: Area page for the descent-and-traverse access; route page for the line. No descent stated.

set.approach: Park at either entrance to the powerline trail; both lead to the crag, which sits on the right-hand side of the trail a short walk from the second entrance. Small cliffs appear first and grow into notable ones. The route is on the right side of the powerline trail and easy to spot.

review.notes: Area page for access; route page for the position.

set.approach: The usual approach is from the Long's Peak trailhead on the east side, off Highway 7, going up the Loft and around Clark's Arrow, which is hard to find. The Great White Tower, on which the Great Chimney lies, is the tallest of the Palisade towers and takes centre stage among them. The first pitch starts on the opposite side from where a glance suggests, then spirals around the tower to reach the top of the finger crack and the chimney.
set.descent_text: Walk off the Great White Tower and down the Loft; no rappel is needed. The alternative from the Palisades is to rappel into the Notch at the top of the Notch Couloir.

review.notes: Route page: approach via the Loft and walk-off; area page: descent by the Loft or into the Notch.

set.approach: This line is on the Pericle, a granite formation not far below the summit of Pikes Peak. The route opens with a wide corner that leads to the foot of a clear hand crack.

review.notes: Route page and Pericle area page, which carry no approach text. Where the line sits and the walk back to the top are all that is stated.

set.approach: Hike from the Wild Basin trailhead past the west shore of Thunder Lake, then turn north to Falcon Lake, which lies right below the peak. The route is on the west flank, where the mountain reaches the divide. Find the small buttress on the lower right of the peak, set apart by a small gully on either side, and start up the middle of it, then follow the path of least resistance toward the right-hand peak.
set.descent_text: From the top, hike down to Boulder-Grand Pass, keeping left of the snowfield (facing downhill) to pick up the trail to the Lake of Many Winds, then return to Falcon Lake.

review.notes: Route page for the start and descent; area page for the Wild Basin trail approach.

set.approach: The Possibility Area can be reached from the Mount Blue Sky road by hiking to the notch just right of a minor outcrop to the southwest and rappelling into the feature, or from Echo Lake by the Chicago Lakes trail and then left at the fork toward the outcrop in the meadow. This route starts at a bolted belay on the midway ledge of the Possibility Wall, climbs a corner to a rest, and then traverses an undulating rail.

review.notes: Area-level approach from the Possibility Area page; route page gives the position on the wall. No descent stated.

set.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. Fifth Element climbs the southeast face of Tower 5, starting at the centre of the face just left of a prominent right-facing dihedral that leads to a huge white roof, then angling right toward a big left-facing dihedral.
set.descent_text: Scramble off the tower by a fourth-class line and head south down the obvious gully on the left side of Tower 5, keeping to skier's right where it splits. Steep grassy slopes lead back to the base.

review.notes: Area page for the lake approach and tower numbering; route page for the start and descent.

set.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. Pika Kombat takes the southeast face of Tower 4, toward its left side. It opens in a small, shallow left-facing dihedral and soon moves right to a distinct crack leading up to a ledge.
set.descent_text: The line is equipped for rappelling, so the descent is made down the route on its anchors.

review.notes: Route page for the start and rappel equipment; area page for approach.

set.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. This line is on Tower 4, starting right under the huge roof splitter that sits high on the wall. An orange pillar lies down and left of that roof; PK, the recommended way to start, takes the pillar's left side, while the original start takes its right.
set.descent_text: From the top, scramble to the summit and then south over the saddle with Tower 5, and descend the gully on the south side behind Tower 5, bearing right when in doubt. A steep third-class grassy meadow leads back to the base. It is also possible to rappel from the top of the roof pitch down the PK line.

review.notes: Route page for the start and both descents; area page for approach.

set.approach: From Grand Lake, the North Inlet trail passes Lake Nokoni and ends at Lake Nanita, with the Ptarmigan Towers as its scenic backdrop; counting from the right, they run from one to five. Rain Dancer climbs the southeast face of Tower 1. It starts a little right of the tower in an obvious left-facing dihedral with a piton near its base, then heads left toward a massive left-facing corner high on the tower.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling the tower's northwest back side from a fixed anchor, or build a rappel anchor from nuts or cams if none is there. Downclimbing may be possible but is likely hard.

review.notes: Route page for start and descent; area page for approach.
